i.e. without Christian faith (specially, a heathen); (passively)
untrustworthy (person), or incredible (thing):--that believeth not,
faithless, incredible thing, infidel, unbeliever(-ing).

572.def:
from 573; singleness, i.e. (subjectively) sincerity (without
dissimulation or self-seeking), or (objectively) generosity (copious
bestowal):--bountifulness, liberal(-ity), simplicity, singleness.

573.def:
probably from 1 (as a particle of union) and the base of 4120;
properly, folded together, i.e. single (figuratively, clear):--single.

574.def:
adverb from 573 (in the objective sense of 572); bountifully;
--liberally.

575.def:
a primary particle; "off," i.e. away (from something near), in various
senses (of place, time, or relation; literal or figurative):--(X
here-)after, ago, at, because of, before, by (the space of), for(-th),
from, in, (out) of, off, (up-)on(-ce), since, with. In composition (as
a prefix) it usually denotes separation, departure, cessation,
completion, reversal, etc.

576.def:
from 575 and the base of 939; literally, to disembark; figuratively,
to eventuate:--become, go out, turn.

577.def: from 575 and 906; to throw off; figuratively, to lose:--cast away.

578.def:
from 575 and 991; to look away from everything else, i.e.
(figuratively) intently regard:--have respect.

579.def:
from 577; cast off, i.e. (figuratively) such as to be rejected:--be
refused.

580.def: from 577; rejection; figuratively, loss:--casting away, loss.

581.def:
past participle of a compound of 575 and 1096; absent, i.e. deceased
(figuratively, renounced):--being dead.

582.def: from 583; an enrollment; by implication, an assessment:--taxing.

583.def:
from 575 and 1125; to write off (a copy or list), i.e. enrol:--tax,
write.

584.def:
from 575 and 1166; to show off, i.e. exhibit; figuratively, to
demonstrate, i.e. accredit:--(ap-)prove, set forth, shew.

586.def:
from 575 and 1183; to tithe (as debtor or creditor):--(give, pay,
take) tithe.

588.def:
from 575 and 1209; to take fully, i.e. welcome (persons), approve
(things):--accept, receive (gladly).

589.def:
from 590; to go abroad, i.e. visit a foreign land:--go (travel) into a
far country, journey.

590.def:
from 575 and 1218; absent from one's own people, i.e. a foreign
traveller:--taking a far journey.

591.def:
from 575 and 1325; to give away, i.e. up, over, back, etc. (in various
applications):--deliver (again), give (again), (re-)pay(-ment be
made), perform, recompense, render, requite, restore, reward, sell,
yield.

592.def:
from 575 and a compound of 223 and 3724; to disjoin (by a boundary,
figuratively, a party):--separate.

593.def:
from 575 and 1381; to disapprove, i.e. (by implication) to
repudiate:--disallow, reject.

595.def:
from 659; a laying aside (literally or figuratively):--putting away
(off).

596.def: from 659; a repository, i.e. granary:--barn, garner.

597.def: from 575 and 2343; to treasure away:--lay up in store.

598.def: from 575 and 2346; to crowd (from every side):--press.

599.def:
from 575 and 2348; to die off (literally or figuratively):--be dead,
death, die, lie a-dying, be slain (X with).

600.def:
from 575 and 2525; to reconstitute (in health, home or
organization):--restore (again).

601.def: from 575 and 2572; to take off the cover, i.e. disclose:--reveal.

602.def:
from 601; disclosure:--appearing, coming, lighten, manifestation, be
revealed, revelation.

603.def:
from a comparative of 575 and a compound of kara (the head) and 1380
(in the sense of watching); intense anticipation:--earnest
expectation.

606.def:
from 575 and 2749; to be reserved; figuratively, to await:--be
appointed, (be) laid up.

608.def: from 575 and 2808; to close fully:--shut up.

609.def:
from 575 and 2875; to amputate; reflexively (by irony) to mutilate
(the privy parts):--cut off. Compare 2699.

610.def:
from 611 (in its original sense of judging); a judicial
decision:--sentence.

611.def:
from 575 and krino; to conclude for oneself, i.e. (by implication) to
respond; by Hebraism (compare 6030) to begin to speak (where an
address is expected):--answer.

613.def:
from 575 and 2928; to conceal away (i.e. fully); figuratively, to keep
secret:--hide.

614.def: from 613; secret; by implication, treasured:--hid, kept secret.

615.def:
from 575 and kteino (to slay); to kill outright; figuratively, to
destroy:--put to death, kill, slay.

616.def:
from 575 and the base of 2949; to breed forth, i.e. (by transference)
to generate (figuratively):--beget, produce.

617.def: from 575 and 2947; to roll away:--roll away (back).

618.def:
from 575 and 2983; to receive (specially, in full, or as a host); also
to take aside:--receive, take.

619.def:
from a comparative of 575 and lauo (to enjoy); full
enjoyment:--enjoy(-ment).

620.def:
from 575 and 3007; to leave behind (passively, remain); by
implication, to forsake:--leave, remain.

622.def:
from 575 and the base of 3639; to destroy fully (reflexively, to
perish, or lose), literally or figuratively:--destroy, die, lose, mar,
perish.

623.def: active participle of 622; a destroyer (i.e. Satan):--Apollyon.

624.def:
from the pagan deity Apollon (i.e. the sun; from 622); Apollonia, a
place in Macedonia:--Apollonia.

625.def: probably from the same as 624; Apollos, an Israelite:--Apollos.

626.def:
middle voice from a compound of 575 and 3056; to give an account
(legal plea) of oneself, i.e. exculpate (self):--answer (for self),
make defence, excuse (self), speak for self.

627.def:
from the same as 626; a plea ("apology"):--answer (for self), clearing
of self, defence.

628.def:
from 575 and 3068; to wash fully, i.e. (figuratively) have remitted
(reflexively):--wash (away).

629.def:
from a compound of 575 and 3083; (the act) ransom in full, i.e.
(figuratively) riddance, or (specially) Christian
salvation:--deliverance, redemption.

630.def:
from 575 and 3089; to free fully, i.e. (literally) relieve, release,
dismiss (reflexively, depart), or (figuratively) let die, pardon or
(specially) divorce:--(let) depart, dismiss, divorce, forgive, let go,
loose, put (send) away, release, set at liberty.

631.def:
middle voice from 575 and masso (to squeeze, knead, smear); to scrape
away:--wipe off.

632.def: from 575 and the base of 3551; to apportion, i.e. bestow:--give.

633.def:
from 575 and 3538; to wash off (reflexively, one's own hands
symbolically):--wash.

635.def:
from 575 and 4105; to lead astray (figuratively); passively, to stray
(from truth):--err, seduce.

636.def: from 575 and 4126; to set sail:--sail away.

638.def: from 575 and 4155; to stifle (by drowning or overgrowth):--choke.

639.def:
from a compound of 1 (as a negative particle) and the base of 4198; to
have no way out, i.e. be at a loss (mentally):-- (stand in) doubt, be
perplexed.

640.def: from the same as 639; a (state of) quandary:--perplexity.

641.def: from 575 and 4496; to hurl off, i.e. precipitate (oneself):--cast.

642.def:
from 575 and a derivative of 3737; to bereave wholly, i.e.
(figuratively) separate (from intercourse):--take.

644.def:
from a compound of 575 and a derivative of 4639; a shading off, i.e.
obscuration:--shadow.

645.def:
from 575 and 4685; to drag forth, i.e. (literally) unsheathe (a
sword), or relatively (with a degree of force implied) retire
(personally or factiously):--(with-)draw (away), after we were gotten
from.

646.def:
feminine of the same as 647; defection from truth (properly, the
state) ("apostasy"):--falling away, forsake.

647.def:
neuter of a (presumed) adjective from a derivative of 868; properly,
something separative, i.e. (specially) divorce:--(writing of)
divorcement.

648.def: from 575 and a derivative of 4721; to unroof:--uncover.

649.def:
from 575 and 4724; set apart, i.e. (by implication) to send out
(properly, on a mission) literally or figuratively:--put in, send
(away, forth, out), set (at liberty).

650.def:
from 575 and stereo (to deprive); to despoil:--defraud, destitute,
kept back by fraud.

653.def:
from 575 and a (presumed) derivative of 4750; to speak off-hand
(properly, dictate), i.e. to catechize (in an invidious
manner):--provoke to speak.

654.def:
from 575 and 4762; to turn away or back (literally or
figuratively):--bring again, pervert, turn away (from).

655.def: from 575 and the base of 4767; to detest utterly:--abhor.

656.def: from 575 and 4864; excommunicated:--(put) out of the synagogue(-s).

657.def:
middle voice from 575 and 5021; literally, to say adieu (by departing
or dismissing); figuratively, to renounce:--bid farewell, forsake,
take leave, send away.

658.def: from 575 and 5055; to complete entirely, i.e. consummate:--finish.

659.def:
from 575 and 5087; to put away (literally or figuratively):--cast off,
lay apart (aside, down), put away (off).

660.def: from 575 and tinasso (to jostle); to brush off:--shake off.

661.def: from 575 and 5099; to pay in full:--repay.

662.def: from 575 and 5111; to venture plainly:--be very bold.

663.def:
from the base of 664; (figuratively) decisiveness, i.e.
rigor:--severity.

664.def:
adverb from a derivative of a comparative of 575 and temno (to cut);
abruptly, i.e. peremptorily:--sharply(-ness).

665.def:
from 575 and the base of 5157; to deflect, i.e. (reflexively)
avoid:--turn away.

666.def: from the participle of 548; a being away:--absence.

667.def:
from 575 and 5342; to bear off (literally or relatively):--bring,
carry (away).

669.def:
from 575 and 5350; to enunciate plainly, i.e. declare:--say, speak
forth, utterance.

670.def: from 575 and the middle voice of 5412; to unload:--unlade.

671.def:
from a compound of 575 and 5530; the act of using up, i.e.
consumption:--using.

673.def:
from 575 and 5563; to rend apart; reflexively, to separate:--depart
(asunder).

674.def: from 575 and 5594; to breathe out, i.e. faint:--hearts failing.

675.def:
of Latin origin; (in the genitive, i.e. possessive case) of Appius,
the name of a Roman:--Appii.

676.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a comparative of
4314 and eimi (to go); inaccessible:--which no man can approach.

678.def:
adverb from a compound of 1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed
derivative of a presumed compound of 4383 and 2983 (compare 4381); in
a way not accepting the person, i.e. impartially:--without respect of
persons.

679.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 4417; not
stumbling, i.e. (figuratively) without sin:--from falling.

680.def:
reflexive of 681; properly, to attach oneself to, i.e. to touch (in
many implied relations):--touch.

681.def:
a primary verb; properly, to fasten to, i.e. (specially) to set on
fire:--kindle, light.

682.def: probably of foreign origin; Apphia, a woman of Collosae:--Apphia.

683.def:
or apothomai ap-o'-thom-ahee

from 575 and the middle voice of otheo or otho (to shove); to push
off, figuratively, to reject:--cast away, put away (from), thrust away
(from).

684.def:
from a presumed derivative of 622; ruin or loss (physical, spiritual
or eternal):--damnable(-nation), destruction, die, perdition, X
perish, pernicious ways, waste.

685.def:
probably from 142; properly, prayer (as lifted to Heaven), i.e. (by
implication) imprecation:--curse.

686.def:
probably from 142 (through the idea of drawing a conclusion); a
particle denoting an inference more or less decisive (as
follows):--haply, (what) manner (of man), no doubt, perhaps, so be,
then, therefore, truly, wherefore. Often used in connection with other
particles, especially 1065 or 3767 (after) or 1487 (before). Compare
also 687.

687.def:
a form of 686, denoting an interrogation to which a negative answer is
presumed:--therefore.

688.def: of Hebrew origin (6152); Arabia, a region of Asia:--Arabia.

689.def: of Hebrew origin (7410); Aram (i.e. Ram), an Israelite:--Aram.

690.def: from 688; an Arab or native of Arabia:--Arabian.

691.def: from 692; to be idle, i.e. (figuratively) to delay:--linger.

692.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and 2041; inactive, i.e. unemployed;
(by implication) lazy, useless:--barren, idle, slow.

694.def:
neuter of a presumed derivative of 696; silvery, i.e. (by implication)
cash; specially, a silverling (i.e. drachma or shekel):--money, (piece
of) silver (piece).

695.def: from 696 and 2875; a beater (i.e. worker) of silver:--silversmith.

696.def:
from argos (shining); silver (the metal, in the articles or
coin):--silver.

697.def:
from Ares (the name of the Greek deity of war) and a derivative of
4078; rock of Ares, a place in Athens:--Areopagus, Mars' Hill.

698.def:
from 697; an Areopagite or member of the court held on Mars'
Hill:--Areopagite.

700.def:
probably from 142 (through the idea of exciting emotion); to be
agreeable (or by implication, to seek to be so):--please.

701.def:
from 700; agreeable; by implication, fit:--(things that) please(-ing),
reason.

702.def: of foreign origin; Aretas, an Arabian:--Aretas.

703.def:
from the same as 730; properly, manliness (valor), i.e. excellence
(intrinsic or attributed):--praise, virtue.

704.def: perhaps the same as 730; a lamb (as a male):--lamb.

707.def:
of Hebrew origin (7414); Arimathaea (or Ramah), a place in
Palestine:--Arimathaea.

708.def:
from the same as 712 and 757; best ruling; Aristarchus, a
Macedonian:--Aristarchus.

709.def: from 712; to take the principle meal:--dine.

710.def:
apparently a comparative of the same as 712; the left hand (as
second-best):--left (hand).

711.def:
from the same as 712 and 1012; best counselling; Aristoboulus, a
Christian:--Aristobulus.

712.def:
apparently neuter of a superlative from the same as 730; the best meal
(or breakfast; perhaps from eri ("early")), i.e. luncheon:--dinner.

714.def:
apparently a primary verb (but probably akin to 142 through the idea
of raising a barrier); properly, to ward off, i.e. (by implication) to
avail (figuratively, be satisfactory):--be content, be enough,
suffice, be sufficient.

715.def: probably from 714; a bear (as obstructing by ferocity):--bear.

716.def:
probably from 142 (perhaps with 1 (as a particle of union) prefixed);
a chariot (as raised or fitted together (compare 719)):--chariot.

717.def:
of Hebrew origin (2022 and 4023); Armageddon (or Har-Meggiddon), a
symbolic name:--Armageddon.

718.def:
from 719; to joint, i.e. (figuratively) to woo (reflexively, to
betroth):--espouse.

719.def: from the same as 716; an articulation (of the body):--joint.

720.def:
perhaps from 1 (as a negative particle) and the middle voice of 4483;
to contradict, i.e. disavow, reject, abnegate:--deny, refuse.

726.def:
from a derivative of 138; to seize (in various applications):--catch
(away, up), pluck, pull, take (by force).

728.def:
of Hebrew origin (6162); a pledge, i.e. part of the purchase-money or
property given in advance as security for the rest:--earnest.

729.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of the same
as 4476; unsewed, i.e. of a single piece:--without seam.

730.def:
or arsen ar'-sane

probably from 142; male (as stronger for lifting):--male, man.

731.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and the same as 4490; unsaid, i.e. (by
implication) inexpressible:--unspeakable.

732.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of 4517;
infirm:--sick (folk, -ly).

733.def:
from 730 and 2845; a sodomite:--abuser of (that defile) self with
mankind.

734.def:
contracted from a compound of 735 and 1435; gift of Artemis; Artemas
(or Artemidorus), a Christian:--Artemas.

736.def:
from a derivative of 737; properly, something ready (or else more
remotely from 142 (compare 740); something hung up), i.e. (specially)
the topsail (rather foresail or jib) of a vessel:--mainsail.

737.def:
adverb from a derivative of 142 (compare 740) through the idea of
suspension; just now:--this day (hour), hence(-forth), here(-after),
hither(-to), (even) now, (this) present.

738.def:
from 737 and 1084; just born, i.e. (figuratively) a young
convert:--new born.

740.def: from 142; bread (as raised) or a loaf:--(shew-)bread, loaf.

741.def:
from a presumed derivative of 142; to prepare, i.e. spice (with
stimulating condiments):--season.

742.def:
of Hebrew origin (775); Arphaxad, a post-diluvian
patriarch:--Arphaxad.

745.def:
from 757 and 2994; people-ruling; Archelaus, a Jewish
king:--Archelaus.

746.def:
from 756; (properly abstract) a commencement, or (concretely) chief
(in various applications of order, time, place, or rank):--beginning,
corner, (at the, the) first (estate), magistrate, power, principality,
principle, rule.

747.def: from 746 and 71; a chief leader:--author, captain, prince.

748.def: from 746 and a derivative of 2413; high-priestly:--of the high-priest.

750.def: from 746 and 4166; a head shepherd:--chief shepherd.

751.def: from 746 and 2462; horse-ruler; Archippus, a Christian:--Archippus.

752.def:
from 746 and 4864; director of the synagogue services:--(chief) ruler
of the synagogue.

753.def:
from 746 and 5045; a chief constructor, i.e.
"architect":--masterbuilder.

754.def:
from 746 and 5057; a principle tax-gatherer:--chief among the
publicans.

755.def:
from 746 and a compound of 5140 and 2827 (a dinner-bed, because
composed of three couches); director of the entertainment:--governor
(ruler) of the feast.

756.def:
middle voice of 757 (through the implication, of precedence); to
commence (in order of time):--(rehearse from the) begin(-ning).

757.def:
a primary verb; to be first (in political rank or power):--reign
(rule) over.

758.def:
present participle of 757; a first (in rank or power):--chief (ruler),
magistrate, prince, ruler.

759.def:
from 142 (in the sense of sending off scent); an aromatic:--(sweet)
spice.

762.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 4570; not
extinguished, i.e. (by implication) perpetual:--not to be quenched,
unquenchable.

764.def:
from 765; to be (by implied act) impious or wicked:--commit (live,
that after should live) ungodly.

765.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of 4576;
irreverent, i.e. (by extension) impious or wicked:-- ungodly (man).

766.def:
from a compound of 1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed
selges (of uncertain derivation, but apparently meaning
continent); licentiousness (sometimes including other
vices):--filthy, lasciviousness, wantonness.

767.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and the base of 4591; unmarked, i.e.
(figuratively) ignoble:--mean.

768.def: of Hebrew origin (836); Aser (i.e. Asher), an Israelite tribe:--Aser.

769.def:
from 772; feebleness (of mind or body); by implication, malady;
morally, frailty:--disease, infirmity, sickness, weakness.

770.def:
from 772; to be feeble (in any sense):--be diseased, impotent folk
(man), (be) sick, (be, be made) weak.

772.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and the base of 4599; strengthless (in
various applications, literal, figurative and moral):--more feeble,
impotent, sick, without strength, weak(-er, -ness, thing).

773.def:
of uncertain derivation; Asia, i.e. Asia Minor, or (usually) only its
western shore:--Asia.

774.def: from 773; an Asian (i.e. Asiatic) or an inhabitant of Asia:--of Asia.

775.def:
from 773 and 746; an Asiarch or president of the public festivities in
a city of Asia Minor:--chief of Asia.

777.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and 4621; without (taking)
food:--fasting.

778.def:
probably from the same as 4632; to elaborate, i.e. (figuratively)
train (by implication, strive):--exercise.

779.def:
from the same as 778; a leathern (or skin) bag used as a
bottle:--bottle.

780.def: adverb from a derivative of the base of 2237; with pleasure:--gladly.

781.def: from 1 (as a negative particle) and 4680; unwise:--fool.

782.def:
from 1 (as a particle of union) and a presumed form of 4685; to enfold
in the arms, i.e. (by implication) to salute, (figuratively) to
welcome:--embrace, greet, salute, take leave.

783.def: from 782; a greeting (in person or by letter):--greeting, salutation.

784.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and 4695; unblemished (physically or
morally):--without spot, unspotted.

785.def:
of uncertain derivation; a buckler (or round shield); used of a
serpent (as coiling itself), probably the "asp":--asp.

787.def: of Latin origin; an assarius or as, a Roman coin:--farthing.

788.def:
neuter comparative of the base of 1451; more nearly, i.e. very
near:--close.

789.def: probably of foreign origin; Assus, a city of Asia MInor:--Assos.

790.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 2476; to be
non-stationary, i.e. (figuratively) homeless:--have no certain
dwelling-place.

791.def: from astu (a city); urbane, i.e. (by implication) handsome:--fair.

792.def:
probably from the base of 4766; a star (as strown over the sky),
literally or figuratively:--star.

793.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of 4741;
unfixed, i.e. (figuratively) vacillating:--unstable.

794.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of
stergo (to cherish affectionately); hard-hearted towards
kindred:--without natural affection.

796.def: from 797; lightning; by analogy, glare:--lightning, bright shining.

797.def: probably from 792; to flash as lightning:--lighten, shine.

798.def:
neuter from 792; properly, a constellation; put for a single star
(natural or artificial):--star.

799.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 4793;
incomparable; Asyncritus, a Christian:--Asyncritos.

800.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and 4859; inharmonious
(figuratively):--agree not.

801.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and 4908; unintelligent; by
implication, wicked:--foolish, without understanding.

802.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 4934; properly,
not agreed, i.e. treacherous to compacts:-- covenant-breaker.

804.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and sphallo (to "fail"); secure
(literally or figuratively):--certain(-ty), safe, sure.

806.def:
adverb from 804; securely (literally or figuratively):--assuredly,
safely.

807.def:
from 809; to be (i.e. act) unbecoming:--behave self uncomely
(unseemly).

808.def:
from 809; an indecency; by implication, the pudenda:--shame, that
which is unseemly.

809.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of 2192 (in
the sense of its congener 4976); properly, shapeless, i.e.
(figuratively) inelegant:--uncomely.

810.def:
from a compound of 1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed
derivative of 4982; properly, unsavedness, i.e. (by implication)
profligacy:--excess, riot.

811.def: adverb from the same as 810; dissolutely:--riotous.

812.def: from 813; to be (i.e. act) irregular:--behave self disorderly.

813.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 5021; unarranged,
i.e. (by implication) insubordinate (religiously):--unruly.

815.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and 5043; childless:--childless,
without children.

817.def:
a particle probably akin to 427; aloof, i.e. apart from (literally or
figuratively):--in the absence of, without.

818.def:
from 820; to render infamous, i.e. (by implication) contemn or
maltreat:--despise, dishonour, suffer shame, entreat shamefully.

819.def:
from 820; infamy, i.e. (subjectively) comparative indignity,
(objectively) disgrace:--dishonour, reproach, shame, vile.

820.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and 5092; (negatively) unhonoured or
(positively) dishonoured:--despised, without honour, less honourable
(comparative degree).

823.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and the base of 5114; uncut, i.e. (by
implication) indivisible (an "atom" of time):-- moment.

824.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and 5117; out of place, i.e.
(figuratively) improper, injurious, wicked:--amiss, harm,
unreasonable.

825.def:
from Attalos (a king of Pergamus); Attaleia, a place in
Pamphylia:--Attalia.

827.def:
of uncertain derivation; a ray of light, i.e. (by implication)
radiance, dawn:--break of day.

828.def:
from Latin ("august"); Augustus, a title of the Roman
emperor:--Augustus.

829.def:
from 846 and the base of 2237; self-pleasing, i.e.
arrogant:--self-willed.

830.def:
from 846 and the same as 140; self-chosen, i.e. (by implication)
voluntary:--of own accord, willing of self.

831.def:
from a compound of 846 and an obsolete hentes (a worker); to act of
oneself, i.e. (figuratively) dominate:--usurp authority over.

833.def:
from the same as 109; a yard (as open to the wind); by implication, a
mansion:--court, (sheep-)fold, hall, palace.

835.def:
middle voice from 833; to pass the night (properly, in the open
air):--abide, lodge.

836.def: from the same as 109; a flute (as blown):--pipe.

837.def:
a prolonged form of a primary verb; to grow ("wax"), i.e. enlarge
(literal or figurative, active or passive):--grow (up), (give the)
increase.

839.def:
from a derivative of the same as 109 (meaning a breeze, i.e. the
morning air); properly, fresh, i.e. (adverb with ellipsis of 2250)
to-morrow:--(to-)morrow, next day.

840.def:
from a (presumed) derivative of the same as 109 (meaning blown); rough
(properly as a gale), i.e. (figuratively) severe:--austere.

841.def:
from 842; self-satisfaction, i.e. (abstractly) contentedness, or
(concretely) a competence:--contentment, sufficiency.

843.def: from 846 and a derivative or 2632; self-condemned:--condemned of self.

844.def:
from 846 and the same as 3155; self-moved ("automatic"), i.e.
spontaneous:--of own accord, of self.

845.def: from 846 and 3700; self-seeing, i.e. an eye-witness:--eye-witness.

846.def:
from the particle au (perhaps akin to the base of 109 through the idea
of a baffling wind) (backward); the reflexive pronoun self, used
(alone or in the comparative 1438) of the third person , and (with the
proper personal pronoun) of the other persons:--her, it(-self), one,
the other, (mine) own, said, (self-), the) same, ((him-, my-, thy-
)self, (your-)selves, she, that, their(-s), them(-selves), there(-at,
- by, -in, -into, -of, -on, -with), they, (these) things, this (man),
those, together, very, which. Compare 848.

848.def:
contracted for 1438; self (in some oblique case or reflexively,
relation):--her (own), (of) him(-self), his (own), of it, thee, their
(own), them(-selves), they.

849.def:
from 846 and 5495; self-handed, i.e. doing personally:--with ... own
hands.

850.def:
from auchmos (probably from a base akin to that of 109) (dust, as
dried by wind); properly, dirty, i.e. (by implication) obscure:--dark.

851.def:
from 575 and 138; to remove (literally or figuratively):--cut (smite)
off, take away.

852.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and 5316; non-apparent):--that is not
manifest.

853.def:
from 852; to render unapparent, i.e. (actively) consume (becloud), or
(passively) disappear (be destroyed):-- corrupt, disfigure, perish,
vanish away.

855.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 5316;
non-manifested, i.e. invisible:--vanished out of sight.

856.def:
from a compound of 575 and the base of 1476; a place of sitting apart,
i.e. a privy:--draught.

857.def:
from a compound of 1 (as a negative particle) and 5339; unsparingness,
i.e. austerity (asceticism):--neglecting.

858.def:
from a compound of 1 (as a negative particle) and phellos (in the
sense of a stone as stubbing the foot); smoothness, i.e.
(figuratively) simplicity:--singleness.

859.def:
from 863; freedom; (figuratively) pardon:--deliverance, forgiveness,
liberty, remission.

861.def:
from 862; incorruptibility; genitive, unending existence;
(figuratively) genuineness:--immortality, incorruption, sincerity.

862.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 5351; undecaying
(in essence or continuance):--not (in-, un-)corruptible, immortal.

863.def:
from 575 and hiemi (to send; an intensive form of eimi, to go); to
send forth, in various applications (as follow):--cry, forgive,
forsake, lay aside, leave, let (alone, be, go, have), omit, put (send)
away, remit, suffer, yield up.

864.def:
from 575 and the base of 2425; to go (i.e. spread) forth (by
rumor):--come abroad.

865.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and 5358; hostile to virtue:--despiser
of those that are good.

866.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and 5366; unavaricious:--without
covetousness, not greedy of filthy lucre.

867.def:
from 864; properly, arrival, i.e. (by implication)
departure:--departing.

870.def:
adverb from a compound of 1 (as a negative particle) and 5401;
fearlessly:--without fear.

871.def: from 575 and 3666; to assimilate closely:--make like.

873.def:
from 575 and 3724; to set off by boundary, i.e. (figuratively) limit,
exclude, appoint, etc.:--divide, separate, sever.

874.def:
from a compound of 575 and 3729; a starting-point, i.e. (figuratively)
an opportunity:--occasion.

875.def: from 876; to froth at the mouth (in epilepsy):--foam.

876.def: apparently a primary word; froth, i.e. slaver:--foaming.

877.def:
from 878; senselessness, i.e. (euphemistically) egotism; (morally)
recklessness:--folly, foolishly(-ness).

878.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and 5424; properly, mindless, i.e.
stupid, (by implication) ignorant, (specially) egotistic,
(practically) rash, or (morally) unbelieving:--fool(-ish), unwise.

879.def:
from a compound of 575 and 5258; properly, to become awake, i.e. (by
implication) to drop (off) in slumber:--fall asleep.

880.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and 5456; voiceless, i.e. mute (by
nature or choice); figuratively, unmeaning:--dumb, without
signification.

881.def: of Hebrew origin (271); Achaz, an Israelite:--Achaz.

882.def:
of uncertain derivation; Achaia (i.e. Greece), a country of
Europe:--Achaia.

883.def: from 882; an Achaian; Achaicus, a Christian:--Achaicus.

884.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of 5483;
thankless, i.e. ungrateful:--unthankful.

885.def: probably of Hebrew origin (compare 3137); Achim, an Israelite:--Achim.

886.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and 5499; unmanufactured, i.e.
inartificial:--made without (not made with) hands.

887.def:
of uncertain derivation; dimness of sight, i.e. (probably) a
cataract:--mist.

888.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 5534 (compare
5532); useless, i.e. (euphemistically) unmeritorious:--unprofitable.

889.def: from 888; to render useless, i.e. spoil:--become unprofitable.

890.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and 5543; inefficient, i.e. (by
implication) detrimental:--unprofitable.

891.def:
or achris akh'-rece; akin to 206 (through the idea of a terminus); (of
time) until or (of place) up to:--as far as, for, in(-to), till,
(even, un-)to, until, while. Compare 3360.

892.def:
perhaps remotely from cheo (to shed forth); chaff (as
diffusive):--chaff.

893.def: from 1 (as a negative particle) and 5579; veracious:--that cannot lie.

894.def:
of uncertain derivation; wormwood (as a type of bitterness, i.e.
(figuratively) calamity):--wormwood.

895.def:
from 1 (as a negative particle) and 5590; lifeless, i.e. inanimate
(mechanical):--without life.

896.def:
of Hebrew origin (1168); Baal, a Phoenician deity (used as a symbol of
idolatry):--Baal.

897.def:
of Hebrew origin (894); Babylon, the capitol of Chaldaea (literally or
figuratively (as a type of tyranny)):-- Babylon.

898.def:
from the same as 899; a step, i.e. (figuratively) grade (of
dignity):--degree.

899.def:
from the same as 901; profundity, i.e. (by implication) extent;
(figuratively) mystery:--deep(-ness, things), depth.

901.def:
from the base of 939; profound (as going down), literally or
figuratively:--deep, very early.

902.def:
a diminutive of a derivative probably of the base of 939; a palm twig
(as going out far):--branch.

903.def:
of Hebrew origin (1109); Balaam, a Mesopotamian (symbolic of a false
teacher):--Balaam.

904.def: of Hebrew origin (1111); Balak, a Moabite:--Balac.

905.def:
probably remotely from 906 (as a depository); a pouch (for
money):--bag, purse.

906.def:
a primary verb; to throw (in various applications, more or less
violent or intense):--arise, cast (out), X dung, lay, lie, pour, put
(up), send, strike, throw (down), thrust. Compare 4496.

907.def:
from a derivative of 911; to immerse, submerge; to make whelmed (i.e.
fully wet); used only (in the New Testament) of ceremonial ablution,
especially (technically) of the ordinance of Christian
baptism:--Baptist, baptize, wash.

910.def: from 907; a baptizer, as an epithet of Christ's forerunner:--Baptist.

911.def:
a primary verb; to whelm, i.e. cover wholly with a fluid; in the New
Testament only in a qualified or special sense, i.e. (literally) to
moisten (a part of one's person), or (by implication) to stain (as
with dye):--dip.

912.def:
of Chaldee origin (1347 and 5); son of Abba; Bar-abbas, an
Israelite:--Barabbas.

913.def: of Hebrew origin (1301); Barak, an Israelite:--Barak.

914.def:
of Hebrew origin (1296); Barachias (i.e. Berechijah), an
Israelite:--Barachias.

915.def:
of uncertain derivation; a foreigner (i.e.
non-Greek):--barbarian(-rous).

916.def: from 926; to weigh down (figuratively):--burden, charge, heavy, press.

918.def:
of Chaldee origin (1247 and 8526); son of Tolmai; Bar-tholomoeus, a
Christian apostle:--Bartholomeus.

919.def:
of Chaldee origin (1247 and 3091); son of Jesus (or Joshua);
Bar-jesus, an Israelite:--Barjesus.

921.def:
of Chaldee origin (1247 and 5029); son of Nabas (i.e. prophecy);
Barnabas, an Israelite:--Barnabas.

923.def:
of Chaldee origin (1247 and probably 6634); son of Sabas (or Tsaba);
Bar-sabas, the name of two Israelites:--Barsabas.

924.def:
of Chaldee origin (1247 and 2931); son of Timoeus (or the unclean);
Bar-timoeus, an Israelite:--Bartimaeus.

926.def:
from the same as 922; weighty, i.e. (fig) burdensome,
grave:--grievous, heavy, weightier.

928.def: from 931; to torture:--pain, toil, torment, toss, vex.

931.def:
perhaps remotely from the same as 939 (through the notion of going to
the bottom); a touch-stone, i.e. (by analogy) torture:--torment.

932.def:
from 935; properly, royalty, i.e. (abstractly) rule, or (concretely) a
realm (literally or figuratively):--kingdom,
+ reign.

935.def:
probably from 939 (through the notion of a foundation of power); a
sovereign (abstractly, relatively, or figuratively):--king.

936.def: from 935; to rule (literally or figuratively):--king, reign.

937.def:
from 935; regal (in relation), i.e. (literally) belonging to (or
befitting) the sovereign (as land, dress, or a courtier), or
(figuratively) preeminent:--king's, nobleman, royal.

939.def:
from baino (to walk); a pace ("base"), i.e. (by implication) the
foot:--foot.

940.def:
akin to 5335; to malign, i.e. (by extension) to fascinate (by false
representations):--bewitch.

941.def:
perhaps remotely derived from the base of 939 (through the idea of
removal); to lift, literally or figuratively (endure, declare,
sustain, receive, etc.):--bear, carry, take up.

942.def: of uncertain derivation; a brier shrub:--bramble, bush.

943.def: of Hebrew origin (1324); a bath, or measure for liquids:--measure.

945.def:
from Battos (a proverbial stammerer) and 3056; to stutter, i.e. (by
implication) to prate tediously:--use vain repetitions.

948.def:
from a (presumed) derivative of bdeo (to stink); to be disgusted, i.e.
(by implication) detest (especially of idolatry):--abhor, abominable.

949.def:
from the base of 939 (through the idea of basality); stable (literally
or figuratively):--firm, of force, stedfast, sure.

952.def:
from the base of 939 and belos (a threshold); accessible (as by
crossing the door-way), i.e. (by implication, of Jewish notions)
heathenish, wicked:--profane (person).

954.def:
of Chaldee origin (by parody on 1176); dung-god; Beelzebul, a name of
Satan:--Beelzebub.

955.def:
of Hebrew origin (1100); worthlessness; Belial, as an epithet of
Satan:--Belial.

956.def: from 906; a missile, i.e. spear or arrow:--dart.

958.def: of Hebrew origin (1144); Benjamin, an Israelite:--Benjamin.

959.def:
from a provincial form of 5342 and 3529; victorious; Bernice, a member
of the Herodian family:--Bernice.

960.def:
perhaps a provincial from a derivative of 4008 (Peroea, i.e. the
region beyond the coast-line); Beroea, a place in Macedonia:--Berea.

961.def: from 960; a Beroeoean or native of Beroea:--of Berea.

963.def:
of Chaldee origin; date-house; Beth-any, a place in
Palestine:--Bethany.

964.def:
of Chaldee origin (compare 1004 and 2617); house of kindness;
Beth-esda, a pool in Jerusalem:--Bethesda.

965.def:
of Hebrew origin (1036); Bethleem (i.e. Beth-lechem), a place in
Palestine:--Bethlehem.

966.def:
of Chaldee origin (compare 1004 and 6719); fishing-house; Bethsaida, a
place in Palestine:--Bethsaida.

967.def:
of Chaldee origin (compare 1004 and 6291); fig-house; Beth-phage, a
place in Palestine:--Bethphage.

968.def:
from the base of 939; a step, i.e. foot-breath; by implication, a
rostrum, i.e. a tribunal:--judgment-seat, set (foot) on, throne.

970.def:
probably akin to 970 (through the idea of vital activity);
force:--violence.

971.def:
from 979; to force, i.e. (reflexively) to crowd oneself (into), or
(passively) to be seized:--press, suffer violence.

974.def: a diminutive of 975; a booklet:--little book.

975.def: a diminutive of 976; a roll:--bill, book, scroll, writing.

976.def:
properly, the inner bark of the papyrus plant, i.e. (by implication) a
sheet or scroll of writing:--book.

977.def:
a reduplicated and prolonged form of an obsolete primary verb (perhaps
causative of 1006); to eat:--eat.

978.def: of uncertain derivation; Bithynia, a region of Asia:--Bithynia.

979.def:
a primary word; life, i.e. (literally) the present state of existence;
by implication, the means of livelihood:--good, life, living.

981.def:
from 980; living (properly, the act, by implication, the
mode):--manner of life.

982.def:
from a derivative of 980; relating to the present existence:--of
(pertaining to, things that pertain to) this life.

984.def:
a primary verb; properly, to hinder, i.e. (by implication) to
injure:--hurt.

985.def:
from blastos (a sprout); to germinate; by implication, to yield
fruit:--bring forth, bud, spring (up).

986.def:
perhaps the same as the base of 985; Blastus, an officer of Herod
Agrippa:--Blastus.

987.def:
from 989; to vilify; specially, to speak impiously:--(speak)
blaspheme(-er, -mously, -my), defame, rail on, revile, speak evil.

988.def:
from 989; vilification (especially against God):--blasphemy, evil
speaking, railing.

989.def:
from a derivative of 984 and 5345; scurrilious, i.e. calumnious
(against men), or (specially) impious (against
God):--blasphemer(-mous), railing.

990.def:
from 991; vision (properly concrete; by implication,
abstract):--seeing.

991.def:
a primary verb; to look at (literally or figuratively):--behold,
beware, lie, look (on, to), perceive, regard, see, sight, take heed.
Compare 3700.

992.def: from 906; fit to be cast (i.e. applied):--must be put.

993.def:
of Chaldee origin (1123 and 7266); sons of commotion; Boanerges, an
epithet of two of the apostles:--Boanerges.

994.def:
apparently a prolonged form of a primary verb; to halloo, i.e. shout
(for help or in a tumultuous way):--cry.

995.def: from 994; a halloo, i.e. call (for aid, etc.):--cry.

996.def:
from 998; aid; specially, a rope or chain for frapping a
vessel:--help.

997.def: from 998; to aid or relieve:--help, succor.

998.def: from 995 and theo (to run); a succorer:--helper.

999.def:
akin to 900; a hole (in the ground); specially, a cistern:--ditch,
pit.

1000.def: from 906; a throw (as a measure of distance):--cast.

1003.def: of Hebrew origin (1162); Booz, (i.e. Boaz), an Israelite:--Booz.

1005.def: of uncertain derivation; the north (properly, wind):--north.

1006.def:
a prolonged form of a primary verb (compare 977, 1016); to pasture; by
extension to, fodder; reflexively, to graze:--feed, keep.

1007.def: of Hebrew origin (1160); Bosor (i.e. Beor), a Moabite:--Bosor.

1009.def:
of uncertain derivation; a bunch (of grapes):--(vine) cluster (of the
vine).

1010.def:
from 1011; an adviser, i.e. (specially) a councillor or member of the
Jewish Sanhedrin:--counsellor.

1011.def:
from 1012; to advise, i.e. (reflexively) deliberate, or (by
implication) resolve:--consult, take counsel, determine, be minded,
purpose.

1012.def:
from 1014; volition, i.e. (objectively) advice, or (by implication)
purpose:--+ advise, counsel, will.

1014.def:
middle voice of a primary verb; to "will," i.e. (reflexively) be
willing:--be disposed, minded, intend, list, (be, of own) will (-ing).
Compare 2309.

1015.def: probably of foreign origin; a hillock:--hill.

1016.def:
probably from the base of 1006; an ox (as grazing), i.e. an animal of
that species ("beef"):--ox.

1017.def:
from brabeus (an umpire of uncertain derivation); an award (of
arbitration), i.e. (specially) a prize in the public games:--prize.

1018.def:
from the same as 1017; to arbitrate, i.e. (genitive case) to govern
(figuratively, prevail):--rule.

1020.def: from 1021 and a prolonged form of 4126; to sail slowly:--sail slowly.

1021.def: of uncertain affinity; slow; figuratively, dull:--slow.

1023.def:
properly, comparative of 1024, but apparently in the sense of
brasso (to wield); the arm, i.e. (figuratively)
strength:--arm.

1024.def:
of uncertain affinity; short (of time, place, quantity, or
number):--few words, little (space, while).

1025.def:
of uncertain affinity; an infant (properly, unborn) literally or
figuratively:--babe, (young) child, infant.

1026.def:
a primary verb; to moisten (especially by a shower):--(send) rain,
wash.

1031.def: a primary verb; to grate the teeth (in pain or rage):--gnash.

1032.def:
a primary verb; to swell out, i.e. (by implication) to gush:--send
forth.

1033.def:
from the base of 977; food (literally or figuratively), especially
(ceremonially) articles allowed or forbidden by the Jewish law:--meat,
victuals.

1036.def: from 1037; to sink; by implication, to drown:--begin to sink, drown.

1037.def: a variation of 899; depth, i.e. (by implication) the sea:--deep.

1039.def: from 1040; made of linen (neuter a linen cloth):--fine linen.

1040.def: of Hebrew origin (948); white linen:--fine linen.

1041.def:
from the base of 939; properly, a stand, i.e. (specially) an
altar:--altar.

1042.def:
of Chaldee origin (compare 1355); the knoll; gabbatha, a vernacular
term for the Roman tribunal in Jerusalem:-- Gabbatha.

1043.def: of Hebrew origin (1403); Gabriel, an archangel:--Gabriel.

1045.def: of Hebrew origin (1410); Gad, a tribe of Israelites:--Gad.

1046.def:
from Gadara (a town east of the Jordan); a Gadarene or inhabitant of
Gadara:--Gadarene.

1048.def:
of Hebrew origin (5804); Gazah (i.e. Azzah), a place in
Palestine:--Gaza.

1049.def:
from 1047 and 5438; a treasure-house, i.e. a court in the temple for
the collection-boxes:--treasury.

1050.def: of Latin origin; Gaius (i.e. Caius), a Christian:--Gaius.

1052.def: from 1053; a Galatian or inhabitant of Galatia:--Galatian.

1053.def: of foreign origin; Galatia, a region of Asia:--Galatia.

1054.def: from 1053; Galatic or relating to Galatia:--of Galatia.

1056.def:
of Hebrew origin (1551); Galiloea (i.e. the heathen circle), a region
of Palestine:--Galilee.

1057.def: from 1056; Galilean or belonging to Galilea:--Galilean, of Galilee.

1058.def: of Latin origin; Gallion (i.e. Gallio), a Roman officer:--Gallio.

1059.def:
of Hebrew origin (1583); Gamaliel (i.e. Gamliel), an
Israelite:--Gamaliel.

1060.def: from 1062; to wed (of either sex):--marry (a wife).

1061.def: from 1062; to espouse (a daughter to a husband):--give in marriage.

1063.def:
a primary particle; properly, assigning a reason (used in argument,
explanation or intensification; often with other particles):--and, as,
because (that), but, even, for, indeed, no doubt, seeing, then,
therefore, verily, what, why, yet.

1064.def:
of uncertain derivation; the stomach; by analogy, the matrix;
figuratively, a gourmand:--belly, + with child, womb.

1065.def:
a primary particle of emphasis or qualification (often used with other
particles prefixed):--and besides, doubtless, at least, yet.

1066.def:
of Hebrew origin (1439); Gedeon (i.e. Gid(e)on), an Israelite:--Gedeon
(in the King James Version).

1068.def:
of Chaldee origin (compare 1660 and 8081); oil-press; Gethsemane, a
garden near Jerusalem:--Gethsemane.

1069.def:
from 1093; a neighbour (as adjoining one's ground); by implication, a
friend:--neighbour.

1070.def:
of uncertain affinity; to laugh (as a sign of joy or
satisfaction):--laugh.

1071.def: from 1070; laughter (as a mark of gratification):--laughter.

1072.def: transitive from 1073; to fill entirely:--fill (be) full.

1073.def: a primary verb; to swell out, i.e. be full:--be full.

1074.def:
from (a presumed derivative of) 1085; a generation; by implication, an
age (the period or the persons):--age, generation, nation, time.

1075.def:
from 1074 and 3056; to reckon by generations, i.e. trace in
genealogy:--count by descent.

1076.def:
from the same as 1075; tracing by generations, i.e.
"genealogy":--genealogy.

1077.def: neuter plural of a derivative of 1078; birthday ceremonies:--birthday.

1078.def:
from the same as 1074; nativity; figuratively, nature:--generation,
nature(-ral).

1079.def: feminine of a presumed derivative of the base of 1074; birth:--birth.

1080.def:
from a variation of 1085; to procreate (properly, of the father, but
by extension of the mother); figuratively, to regenerate:--bear,
beget, be born, bring forth, conceive, be delivered of, gender, make,
spring.

1081.def:
from 1080; offspring; by analogy, produce (literally or
figuratively):--fruit, generation.

1082.def:
of Hebrew origin (compare 3672); Gennesaret (i.e. Kinnereth), a lake
and plain in Palestine:--Gennesaret.

1086.def:
of Hebrew origin (1622); a Gergesene (i.e. Girgashite) or one of the
aborigines of Palestine:--Gergesene.

1087.def:
from 1088; the eldership, i.e. (collectively) the Jewish
Sanhedrin:--senate.

1089.def:
a primary verb; to taste; by implication, to eat; figuratively, to
experience (good or ill):--eat, taste.

1091.def:
neuter of a (presumed) derivative of 1092; cultivable, i.e. a
farm:--husbandry.

1092.def:
from 1093 and the base of 2041; a land-worker, i.e.
farmer:--husbandman.

1093.def:
contracted from a primary word; soil; by extension a region, or the
solid part or the whole of the terrene globe (including the occupants
in each application):--country, earth(-ly), ground, land, world.

1096.def:
a prolongation and middle voice form of a primary verb; to cause to be
("gen"-erate), i.e. (reflexively) to become (come into being), used
with great latitude (literal, figurative, intensive, etc.):--arise, be
assembled, be(-come, -fall, -have self), be brought (to pass), (be)
come (to pass), continue, be divided, draw, be ended, fall, be
finished, follow, be found, be fulfilled, + God forbid, grow, happen,
have, be kept, be made, be married, be ordained to be, partake, pass,
be performed, be published, require, seem, be showed, X soon as it
was, sound, be taken, be turned, use, wax, will, would, be wrought.

1097.def:
a prolonged form of a primary verb; to "know" (absolutely) in a great
variety of applications and with many implications (as follow, with
others not thus clearly expressed):--allow, be aware (of), feel,
(have) know(-ledge), perceived, be resolved, can speak, be sure,
understand.

1098.def:
akin to 1099; sweet wine, i.e. (properly) must (fresh juice), but used
of the more saccharine (and therefore highly inebriating) fermented
wine:--new wine.

1099.def:
of uncertain affinity; sweet (i.e. not bitter nor salt):--sweet,
fresh.

1100.def:
of uncertain affinity; the tongue; by implication, a language
(specially, one naturally unacquired):--tongue.

1101.def:
from 1100 and the base of 2889; properly, a case (to keep mouthpieces
of wind-instruments in) i.e. (by extension) a casket or (specially)
purse:--bag.

1102.def:
by variation for a derivative from knapto (to tease cloth); a
cloth-dresser:--fuller.

1103.def:
from the same as 1077; legitimate (of birth), i.e. genuine:--own,
sincerity, true.

1105.def: akin to 3509; gloom (as of a storm):--blackness.

1107.def:
from a derivative of 1097; to make known; subjectively, to
know:--certify, declare, make known, give to understand, do to wit,
wot.

1108.def:
from 1097; knowing (the act), i.e. (by implication)
knowledge:--knowledge, science.

1110.def: from 1097; well-known:--acquaintance, (which may be) known, notable.

1114.def:
from goao (to wail); properly, a wizard (as muttering spells), i.e.
(by implication) an imposter:--seducer.

1115.def:
of Chaldee origin (compare 1538); the skull; Golgotha, a knoll near
Jerusalem:--Golgotha.

1116.def:
of Hebrew origin (6017); Gomorrha (i.e. Amorah), a place near the Dead
Sea:--Gomorrha.

1117.def:
from 1073; a load (as filling), i.e. (specially) a cargo, or (by
extension) wares:--burden, merchandise.

1118.def: from the base of 1096; a parent:--parent.

1120.def:
from a compound of 1119 and the alternate of 4098; to fall on the
knee:--bow the knee, kneel down.

1121.def:
from 1125; a writing, i.e. a letter, note, epistle, book, etc.; plural
learning:--bill, learning, letter, scripture, writing, written.

1122.def:
from 1121. a writer, i.e. (professionally) scribe or
secretary:--scribe, town-clerk.

1124.def:
a document, i.e. holy Writ (or its contents or a statement in
it):--scripture.

1125.def:
a primary verb; to "grave", especially to write; figuratively, to
describe:--describe, write(-ing, -ten).

1126.def:
from graus (an old woman) and 1491; crone-like, i.e. silly:--old
wives'.

1127.def:
from 1453; to keep awake, i.e. watch (literally or figuratively):--be
vigilant, wake, (be) watch(-ful).

1128.def:
from 1131; to practise naked (in the games), i.e. train
(figuratively):--exercise.

1130.def:
from a derivative of 1131; to strip, i.e. (reflexively) go poorly
clad:--be naked.

1131.def:
of uncertain affinity; nude (absolute or relative, literal or
figurative):--naked.

1133.def: a diminutive from 1135; a little (i.e. foolish) woman:--silly woman.

1135.def:
probably from the base of 1096; a woman; specially, a wife:--wife,
woman.

1136.def:
of Hebrew origin (1463); Gog, a symbolic name for some future
Antichrist:--Gog.

1137.def: probably akin to 1119; an angle:--corner, quarter.

1138.def:
of Hebrew origin (1732); Dabid (i.e. David), the Israelite
king:--David.

1139.def:
middle voice from 1142; to be exercised by a dæmon:--have a (be vexed
with, be possessed with) devil(-s).

1140.def:
neuter of a derivative of 1142; a dæmonic being; by extension a
deity:--devil, god.

1142.def:
from daio (to distribute fortunes); a dæmon or supernatural spirit (of
a bad nature):--devil.

1143.def:
a prolonged form of a primary root; to bite, i.e. (figuratively)
thwart:--bite.

1144.def:
or dakruon dak'-roo-on

of uncertain affinity; a tear:--tear.

1148.def:
probably of Chaldee origin; Dalmanutha, a place in
Palestine:--Dalmanutha.

1149.def:
probably of foreign derivation; Dalmatia, a region of
Europe:--Dalmatia.

1150.def:
a variation of an obsolete primary of the same meaning; to
tame:--tame.

1151.def: probably from the base of 1150; a heifer (as tame):--heifer.

1152.def:
probably from the base of 1150; perhaps gentle; Damaris, an Athenian
woman:--Damaris.

1153.def: from 1154; a Damascene or inhabitant of Damascus:--Damascene.

1154.def: of Hebrew origin (1834); Damascus, a city of Syria:--Damascus.

1155.def: from 1156; to loan on interest; reflexively, to borrow:--borrow, lend.

1156.def: from danos (a gift); probably akin to the base of 1325; a loan:--debt.

1158.def: of Hebrew origin (1840); Daniel, an Israelite:--Daniel.

1159.def:
from 1160; to expend, i.e. (in a good sense) to incur cost, or (in a
bad one) to waste:--be at charges, consume, spend.

1161.def:
a primary particle (adversative or continuative); but, and,
etc.:--also, and, but, moreover, now (often unexpressed in English).

1163.def:
3d person singular active present of 1210; also deon deh-on'; neuter
active participle of the same; both used impersonally; it is (was,
etc.) necessary (as binding):--behoved, be meet, must (needs), (be)
need(-ful), ought, should.

1164.def: from the base of 1166; a specimen (as shown):--example.

1166.def:
a prolonged form of an obsolete primary of the same meaning; to show
(literally or figuratively):--shew.

1169.def: from deos (dread); timid, i.e. (by implication) faithless:--fearful.

1170.def:
probably from the same as 1171 (through the idea of forgetting the
name as fearful, i.e. strange); so and so (when the person is not
specified):--such a man.

1171.def:
adverb from a derivative of the same as 1169; terribly, i.e.
excessively:--grievously, vehemently.

1172.def:
from 1173; to dine, i.e. take the principle (or evening) meal:--sup (X
-er).

1173.def:
from the same as 1160; dinner, i.e. the chief meal (usually in the
evening):--feast, supper.

1174.def:
the compound of a derivative of the base of 1169 and 1142; more
religious than others:--too superstitious.

1178.def: from 1176 and 4002; ten and five, i.e. fifteen:--fifteen.

1179.def:
from 1176 and 4172; the ten-city region; the Decapolis, a district in
Syria:--Decapolis.

1180.def: from 1176 and 5064; ten and four, i.e. fourteen:--fourteen.

1181.def:
feminine of 1182; a tenth, i.e. as a percentage or (technically)
tithe:--tenth (part), tithe.

1183.def:
from 1181; to tithe, i.e. to give or take a tenth:--pay (receive)
tithes.

1185.def:
from the base of 1388; to entrap, i.e. (figuratively) delude:--allure,
beguile, entice.

1186.def: probably from drus (an oak); a tree:--tree.

1187.def:
from 1188 and 2983; a guardsman (as if taking the right) or
light-armed soldier:--spearman.

1188.def:
from 1209; the right side or (feminine) hand (as that which usually
takes):--right (hand, side).

1189.def:
middle voice of 1210; to beg (as binding oneself), i.e.
petition:--beseech, pray (to), make request. Compare 4441.

1190.def: from 1191; a Derbæan or inhabitant of Derbe:--of Derbe.

1191.def: of foreign origin; Derbe, a place in Asia Minor:--Derbe.

1193.def: from 1192; made of hide:--leathern, of a skin.

1194.def:
a primary verb; properly, to flay, i.e. (by implication) to scourge,
or (by analogy) to thrash:--beat, smite.

1195.def:
from a (presumed) derivative of 1196; to be a binder (captor), i.e. to
enchain (a prisoner), to tie on (a load):-- bind.

1198.def: from 1199; a captive (as bound):--in bonds, prisoner.

1199.def:
or desmos des-mos'

neuter and masculine respectively from 1210; a band, i.e. ligament (of
the body) or shackle (of a prisoner); figuratively, an impediment or
disability:--band, bond, chain, string.

1200.def:
from 1199 and 5441; a jailer (as guarding the prisoners):--jailor,
keeper of the prison.

1201.def:
from a derivative of 1199 (equivalent to 1196); a place of bondage,
i.e. a dungeon:--prison.

1202.def: from the same as 1201; (passively) a captive:--prisoner.

1203.def:
perhaps from 1210 and posis (a husband); an absolute ruler
("despot"):--Lord, master.

1204.def:
of uncertain affinity; here; used also imperative hither!; and of
time, hitherto:--come (hither), hither(-to).

1205.def:
from 1204 and an imperative form of eimi (to go); come hither!:--come,
X follow.

1206.def: from 1208; secondary, i.e. (specially) on the second day:--next day.

1208.def:
as the compare of 1417; (ordinal) second (in time, place, or rank;
also adverb):--afterward, again, second(-arily, time).

1209.def:
middle voice of a primary verb; to receive (in various applications,
literally or figuratively):--accept, receive, take. Compare 2983.

1210.def:
a primary verb; to bind (in various applications, literally or
figuratively):--bind, be in bonds, knit, tie, wind. See also 1163,
1189.

1211.def:
probably akin to 1161; a particle of emphasis or explicitness; now,
then, etc.:--also, and, doubtless, now, therefore.

1212.def: of uncertain derivation; clear:--+ bewray, certain, evident, manifest.

1213.def: from 1212; to make plain (by words):--declare, shew, signify.

1215.def:
from a compound of 1218 and 58; to be a people-gatherer, i.e. to
address a public assembly:--make an oration.

1216.def:
from Demeter (Ceres); Demetrius, the name of an Ephesian and of a
Christian:--Demetrius.

1217.def:
from 1218 and 2041; a worker for the people, i.e. mechanic (spoken of
the Creator):--maker.

1218.def: from 1210; the public (as bound together socially):--people.

1219.def:
from 1218; public; (feminine singular dative case as adverb) in
public:--common, openly, publickly.

1220.def: of Latin origin; a denarius (or ten asses):--pence, penny(-worth).

1222.def:
from 1211 and 4225; a particle of asseveration; indeed
doubtless:--verily.

1223.def:
a primary preposition denoting the channel of an act; through (in very
wide applications, local, causal, or occasional):--after, always,
among, at, to avoid, because of (that), briefly, by, for (cause) ...
fore, from, in, by occasion of, of, by reason of, for sake, that,
thereby, therefore, X though, through(-out), to, wherefore, with
(-in). In composition it retains the same general importance.

1224.def: from 1223 and the base of 939; to cross:--come over, pass (through).

1226.def:
middle voice of a compound of 1223 and 950; to confirm thoroughly (by
words), i.e. asseverate:--affirm constantly.

1227.def:
from 1223 and 991; to look through, i.e. recover full vision:--see
clearly.

1228.def:
from 1225; a traducer; specially, Satan (compare 7854):--false
accuser, devil, slanderer.

1229.def:
from 1223 and the base of 32; to herald thoroughly:--declare, preach,
signify.

1230.def: from 1223 and 1096; to elapse meanwhile:--X after, be past, be spent.

1231.def:
from 1223 and 1097; to know thoroughly, i.e. ascertain
exactly:--(would) enquire, know the uttermost.

1234.def: from 1223 and 1111; to complain throughout a crowd:--murmur.

1235.def: from 1223 and 1127; to waken thoroughly:--be awake.

1236.def: from 1223 and 71; to pass time or life:--lead life, living.

1237.def:
from 1223 and 1209; to receive in turn, i.e. (figuratively) succeed
to:--come after.

1238.def:
from a compound of 1223 and 1210; a "diadem" (as bound about the
head):--crown. Compare 4735.

1239.def:
from 1223 and 1325; to give throughout a crowd, i.e. deal out; also to
deliver over (as to a successor):--(make) distribute(-ion), divide,
give.

1242.def:
from 1303; properly, a disposition, i.e. (specially) a contract
(especially a devisory will):--covenant, testament.

1243.def:
from 1244; a distinction or (concretely) variety:--difference,
diversity.

1244.def: from 1223 and 138; to separate, i.e. distribute:--divide.

1245.def:
from 1223 and 2511; to cleanse perfectly, i.e. (specially)
winnow:--thoroughly purge.

1246.def:
middle voice from 1223 and a compound of 2596 and 1651; to prove
downright, i.e. confute:--convince.

1248.def:
from 1249; attendance (as a servant, etc.); figuratively
(eleemosynary) aid, (official) service (especially of the Christian
teacher, or technically of the diaconate):--(ad-)minister(-ing,
-tration, -try), office, relief, service(-ing).

1249.def:
probably from an obsolete diako (to run on errands; compare 1377); an
attendant, i.e. (genitive case) a waiter (at table or in other menial
duties); specially, a Christian teacher and pastor (technically, a
deacon or deaconess):--deacon, minister, servant.

1251.def:
middle voice from 1223 and 191; to hear throughout, i.e. patiently
listen (to a prisoner's plea):--hear.

1252.def:
from 1223 and 2919; to separate thoroughly, i.e. (literally and
reflexively) to withdraw from, or (by implication) oppose;
figuratively, to discriminate (by implication, decide), or
(reflexively) hesitate:--contend, make (to) differ(-ence), discern,
doubt, judge, be partial, stagger, waver.

1254.def:
from 1223 and 2967; to hinder altogether, i.e. utterly
prohibit:--forbid.

1255.def:
from 1223 and 2980; to talk throughout a company, i.e. converse or
(genitive case) publish:--commune, noise abroad.

1256.def:
middle voice from 1223 and 3004; to say thoroughly, i.e. discuss (in
argument or exhortation):--dispute, preach (unto), reason (with),
speak.

1257.def: from 1223 and 3007; to leave off in the middle, i.e. intermit:--cease.

1258.def: from 1256; a (mode of) discourse, i.e. "dialect":--language, tongue.

1259.def:
from 1223 and 236; to change thoroughly, i.e. (mentally) to
conciliate:--reconcile.

1260.def:
from 1223 and 3049; to reckon thoroughly, i.e. (genitive case) to
deliberate (by reflection or discussion):--cast in mind, consider,
dispute, muse, reason, think.

1263.def:
from 1223 and 3140; to attest or protest earnestly, or (by
implication) hortatively:--charge, testify (unto), witness.

1264.def: from 1223 and 3164; to fight fiercely (in altercation):--strive.

1265.def:
from 1223 and 3306; to stay constantly (in being or
relation):--continue, remain.

1266.def:
from 1223 and 3307; to partition thoroughly (literally in
distribution, figuratively in dissension):--cloven, divide, part.

1268.def:
from 1223 and the base of 3551; to distribute, i.e. (of information)
to disseminate:--spread.

1269.def:
from 1223 and 3506; to nod (or express by signs) across an intervening
space:--beckon.

1270.def:
from a compound of 1223 and 3539; something thought through, i.e. a
sentiment:--thought.

1271.def:
from 1223 and 3563; deep thought, properly, the faculty (mind or its
disposition), by implication, its exercise:-- imagination, mind,
understanding.

1272.def:
from 1223 and 455; to open thoroughly, literally (as a first-born) or
figuratively (to expound):--open.

1273.def:
from 1223 and a derivative of 3571; to sit up the whole
night:--continue all night.

1274.def: from 1223 and anuo (to effect); to accomplish thoroughly:--finish.

1276.def:
from 1223 and a derivative of the base of 4008; to cross entirely:--go
over, pass (over), sail over.

1277.def: from 1223 and 4126; to sail through:--sail over.

1278.def:
from 1223 and a derivative of 4192; to toil through, i.e. (passively)
be worried:--be grieved.

1279.def:
from 1223 and 4198; to travel through:--go through, journey in, pass
by.

1280.def:
from 1223 and 639; to be thoroughly nonplussed:--(be in) doubt, be
(much) perplexed.

1281.def:
from 1223 and 4231; to thoroughly occupy oneself, i.e. (transitively
and by implication) to earn in business:--gain by trading.

1282.def:
from 1223 and the base of 4249; to saw asunder, i.e. (figuratively) to
exasperate:--cut (to the heart).

1283.def: from 1223 and 726; to seize asunder, i.e. plunder:--spoil.

1285.def:
from 1223 and saphes (clear); to clear thoroughly, i.e. (figuratively)
declare:--tell unto.

1286.def:
from 1223 and 4579; to shake thoroughly, i.e. (figuratively) to
intimidate:--do violence to.

1287.def:
from 1223 and 4650; to dissipate, i.e. (genitive case) to rout or
separate; specially, to winnow; figuratively, to squander:--disperse,
scatter (abroad), strew, waste.

1288.def:
from 1223 and 4685; to draw apart, i.e. sever or dismember:--pluck
asunder, pull in pieces.

1289.def:
from 1223 and 4687; to sow throughout, i.e. (figuratively) distribute
in foreign lands:--scatter abroad.

1291.def:
middle voice from 1223 and 4724; to set (oneself) apart (figuratively,
distinguish), i.e. (by implication) to enjoin:--charge, that which was
(give) commanded(-ment).

1294.def:
from 1223 and 4762; to distort, i.e. (figuratively) misinterpret, or
(morally) corrupt:--perverse(-rt), turn away.

1295.def:
from 1223 and 4982; to save thoroughly, i.e. (by implication or
analogy) to cure, preserve, rescue, etc.:--bring safe, escape (safe),
heal, make perfectly whole, save.

1298.def:
from 1223 and 5015; to disturb wholly, i.e. agitate (with
alarm):--trouble.

1299.def:
from 1223 and 5021; to arrange thoroughly, i.e. (specially) institute,
prescribe, etc.:--appoint, command, give, (set in) order, ordain.

1300.def:
from 1223 and 5055; to accomplish thoroughly, i.e. (subjectively) to
persist:--continue.

1301.def:
from 1223 and 5083; to watch thoroughly, i.e. (positively and
transitively) to observe strictly, or (negatively and reflexively) to
avoid wholly:--keep.

1303.def:
middle voice from 1223 and 5087; to put apart, i.e. (figuratively)
dispose (by assignment, compact, or bequest):--appoint, make,
testator.

1304.def:
from 1223 and the base of 5147; to wear through (time), i.e.
remain:--abide, be, continue, tarry.

1305.def: from a compound of 1223 and 5142; nourishment:--food.

1306.def: from 1223 and 826; to glimmer through, i.e. break (as day):--dawn.

1308.def:
from 1223 and 5342; to bear through, i.e. (literally) transport;
usually to bear apart, i.e. (objectively) to toss about (figuratively,
report); subjectively, to "differ", or (by implication) surpass:--be
better, carry, differ from, drive up and down, be (more) excellent,
make matter, publish, be of more value.

1309.def: from 1223 and 5343; to flee through, i.e. escape:--escape.

1310.def:
from 1223 and a derivative of 5345; to report thoroughly, i.e.
divulgate:--blaze abroad, commonly report, spread abroad, fame.

1311.def:
from 1225 and 5351; to rot thoroughly, i.e. (by implication) to ruin
(passively, decay utterly, figuratively, pervert):--corrupt, destroy,
perish.

1313.def:
from 1308; varying; also surpassing:--differing, divers, more
excellent.

1314.def: from 1223 and 5442; to guard thoroughly, i.e. protect:--keep.

1315.def:
from 1223 and a derivative of 5495; to handle thoroughly, i.e. lay
violent hands upon:--kill, slay.

1316.def:
from 1223 and the middle voice of 5563; to remove (oneself) wholly,
i.e. retire:--depart.

1318.def:
from 1321; (subjectively) instructed, or (objectively) communicated by
teaching:--taught, which ... teacheth.

1319.def:
from 1320; instruction (the function or the information):--doctrine,
learning, teaching.

1320.def:
from 1321; an instructor (genitive case or specially):--doctor,
master, teacher.

1321.def:
a prolonged (causative) form of a primary verb dao (to learn); to
teach (in the same broad application):--teach.

1322.def:
from 1321; instruction (the act or the matter):--doctrine, hath been
taught.

1324.def:
prolongation from 1364; double, i.e. twin; Didymus, a
Christian:--Didymus.

1325.def:
a prolonged form of a primary verb (which is used as an alternative in
most of the tenses); to give (used in a very wide application,
properly, or by implication, literally or figuratively; greatly
modified by the connection):--adventure, bestow, bring forth, commit,
deliver (up), give, grant, hinder, make, minister, number, offer, have
power, put, receive, set, shew, smite (+ with the hand), strike (+
with the palm of the hand), suffer, take, utter, yield.

1326.def:
from 1223 and 1453; to wake fully; i.e. arouse (literally or
figuratively):--arise, awake, raise, stir up.

1327.def:
from 1223 and 1841; an outlet through, i.e. probably an open square
(from which roads diverge):--highway.

1329.def:
from 1223 and 2059; to explain thoroughly, by implication, to
translate:--expound, interpret(-ation).

1331.def:
from 1223 and 2065; to question throughout, i.e. ascertain by
interrogation:--make enquiry foreign

1332.def: from 1364 and 2094; of two years (in age):--two years old.

1333.def: from 1332; a space of two years (biennium):--two years.

1334.def: from 1223 and 2233; to relate fully:--declare, shew, tell.

1337.def:
from 1364 and 2281; having two seas, i.e. a sound with a double
